cases.sentence: И нарушает эту тишину лишь сиплый женский ___, льющийся из ниоткуда.
cases.translation: And this silence is broken only by a hoarse woman's bass voice pouring out of nowhere.
cases.explain: Despite standing after the verb, бас is the subject of «нарушает», and subjects take the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я стою как столб посреди площади Курского ___.
cases.translation: I stand like a post in the middle of the square of the Kursk railway station.
cases.explain: The preposition «посреди» always governs the genitive, and here вокзала also depends on the noun площади, which likewise requires the genitive.

cases.sentence: В 8 часов 16 минут из четвертого тупика отправится поезд до ___.
cases.translation: At 8.16 the train to Petushki will leave from the fourth siding.
cases.explain: «До» meaning 'as far as, up to' takes the genitive; Петушки is a plural place name, so its genitive is Петушков.

cases.sentence: Я обращаюсь ко всем ___ доброй воли.
cases.translation: I appeal to all people of good will.
cases.explain: «Обращаться к кому-либо» — the preposition «к» requires the dative, hence ко всем людям.

cases.sentence: Давайте почтим ___ молчания два этих смертных часа.
cases.translation: Let us honour those two deadly hours with a minute of silence.
cases.explain: «Почтить» takes the instrumental for the means by which one honours something: почтить минутой молчания.
«О/об» in the sense of 'about, concerning' is one of the prepositions that only ever governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Я лучше сяду и буду в ___ смотреть.
cases.translation: I would rather sit down and look out of the little window.
cases.explain: «Смотреть в» points the gaze towards something, so «в» takes the accusative; окошко is a neuter inanimate noun, whose accusative matches the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я лучше сяду, к ___ прижму чемоданчик.
cases.translation: I would rather sit down and press the little suitcase to my heart.
cases.explain: «К» expressing motion towards something governs the dative: прижать к сердцу.

reading.question: What does Venichka say about describing what happened between the restaurant and the train?
options: He will not attempt it either
He will describe it in full detail
He will describe it only in Petushki
reading.correct: He will not attempt it either
reading.explain: He says no human tongue could express it, and that he does not undertake it either.

reading.question: What does Venichka tell himself to do about those two deadly hours?
options: Remember them even in his most blissful moments
Forget them as quickly as possible
Write them down in his notebook
reading.correct: Remember them even in his most blissful moments
reading.explain: He orders himself to remember them in his most rapturous days and in moments of bliss.

reading.ru: Если есть у вас под рукой какой-нибудь завалящий гудок – нажмите на этот гудок.
reading.question: What does Venichka ask people to do if they have some worthless old hooter to hand?
reading.explain: He turns the minute of silence into a public ceremony, asking people to press any hooter they have.

reading.question: Where does Venichka stand still for exactly one minute?
options: In the middle of the square outside the Kursk station
On the platform beside the train
At the entrance of a stranger's building
reading.correct: In the middle of the square outside the Kursk station
reading.explain: He stands like a post in the middle of the Kursk station square, staring blearily at the station clock.

reading.ru: Такси обтекают меня со всех четырех сторон.
reading.question: What flows around Venichka from all four sides while he stands still?
reading.explain: Taxis, and people too, stream around the motionless Venichka.

reading.ru: И нарушает эту тишину лишь сиплый женский бас, льющийся из ниоткуда.
reading.question: What is the only thing that breaks the silence?
options: A hoarse woman's bass voice coming from nowhere
reading.correct: A hoarse woman's bass voice coming from nowhere
reading.explain: The voice is the station announcer reading out the departure of the Petushki train.

reading.ru: В 8 часов 16 минут из четвертого тупика отправится поезд до Петушков.
reading.question: When and from where does the train to Petushki depart?
reading.explain: The announcement is repeated twice with exactly these details.

reading.question: What do the voices questioning Venichka first want to know?
options: Whether his little suitcase is heavy now
Whether he has any money left
reading.correct: Whether his little suitcase is heavy now
reading.explain: They ask about the weight of the suitcase and whether a reed pipe is singing in his heart.

reading.ru: А насчет свирели говорить еще рано…
reading.question: How does Venichka answer the question about the reed pipe singing in his heart?
options: That it is still too early to speak of that
That it has been singing since dawn
That the pipe has gone silent for good
reading.correct: That it is still too early to speak of that
reading.explain: He confirms the suitcase is heavy but says the pipe is not yet a subject for discussion.

reading.ru: Да – розовое крепкое за рупь тридцать семь.
reading.question: Which wine does Venichka finally remember buying?
options: Pink fortified wine for a rouble thirty-seven
reading.correct: Pink fortified wine for a rouble thirty-seven
reading.explain: He first says only 'some red one', then recalls it was pink fortified wine at one rouble thirty-seven.

reading.question: What do the two bottles of Kubanskaya and the two quarter-bottles of Rossiyskaya come to together?
reading.explain: He adds five twenty-four for the Kubanskaya to three twenty-eight for the Rossiyskaya.

reading.ru: Но ведь это не совсем общий итог.
reading.question: Why is nine roubles eighty-nine kopecks not quite the final total?
options: Because he also bought two sandwiches
Because he still owes money for the beer
Because he forgot the price of the wine
Because the shop gave him the wrong change
reading.correct: Because he also bought two sandwiches
reading.explain: He adds that he bought two sandwiches as well, so as not to throw up.

reading.ru: Первую дозу я не могу без закуски, потому что могу сблевать.
reading.question: Why does Venichka need something to eat with the very first dose?
options: Because otherwise he might throw up
Because he has not eaten since yesterday
Because the vodka is too cheap
Because his companions insist on it
reading.correct: Because otherwise he might throw up
reading.explain: He explains that only the first dose needs a bite to eat; the second and third he can drink dry.

reading.question: After how many doses will Venichka need a sandwich again?
reading.explain: He says it goes on like that right up to the ninth dose, after which a sandwich is needed once more.

reading.ru: Было б у меня побольше денег, я взял бы еще пива и пару портвейнов, но ведь…
reading.question: What would Venichka have bought if he had had more money?
options: Beer and a couple of bottles of port
A ticket to a further station
reading.correct: Beer and a couple of bottles of port
reading.explain: He answers the mocking question about whether that is all he needs to be happy.

reading.ru: Да я и в ресторане, если хотите, прижимал его к сердцу, а водки там еще не было.
reading.question: How does Venichka argue that clutching the suitcase has nothing to do with vodka?
options: He was already pressing it to his heart in the restaurant, when there was no vodka in it
He says the suitcase contains only sandwiches
He says he never presses it to his heart at all
He says the vodka is in his coat pocket
reading.correct: He was already pressing it to his heart in the restaurant, when there was no vodka in it
reading.explain: He also recalls doing the same in the entrance hall, where there was not even a smell of vodka.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that even angels could say nothing about those two hours?
sentences: Что было потом – от ресторана до магазина и от магазина до поезда – человеческий язык не повернется выразить.
Я тоже не берусь.
А если за это возьмутся ангелы, – они просто расплачутся, а сказать от слез ничего не сумеют.
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the one that brings in the angels, who would only burst into tears.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what Venichka's hair is doing while he stands still?
sentences: Так.
Я тоже останавливаюсь.
Ровно минуту, мутно глядя в вокзальные часы, я стою как столб посреди площади Курского вокзала.
Волосы мои то развеваются на ветру, то дыбом встают, то развеваются снова.
Такси обтекают меня со всех четырех сторон.
Люди – тоже, и смотрят так дико: думают, наверное, – изваять его вот так, в назидание народам древности, или не изваять?
highlight.explain: Only the fourth sentence talks about his hair streaming in the wind and standing on end.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the pink fortified wine among Venichka's purchases?
sentences: Да ведь я понимаю, что интересно.
Сейчас, сейчас перечислю: во-первых, две бутылки кубанской по два шестьдесят две каждая, итого пять двадцать четыре.
Дальше: две четвертинки российской, по рупь шестьдесят четыре, итого пять двадцать четыре плюс три двадцать восемь.
Восемь рублей пятьдесят две копейки.
И еще какое-то красное.
Сейчас, вспомню.
Да – розовое крепкое за рупь тридцать семь.
highlight.explain: He calls it merely 'some red one' at first and only names the pink fortified wine in the last sentence.

highlight.question: Which sentence guesses that Venichka hugs the suitcase because there is vodka inside it?
sentences: Ты не обижайся.
Мы тебе добра хотим.
Только зачем ты, дурак, все к сердцу чемодан прижимаешь?
Потому что водка там, что ли?
highlight.explain: The last sentence supplies the guess about vodka, while the previous one only asks why he does it.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why Venichka cannot take the first dose without something to eat?
sentences: Нет.
Что я сказал, то сказал.
Первую дозу я не могу без закуски, потому что могу сблевать.
А вот уж вторую и третью могу пить всухую, потому что стошнить может и стошнит, но уже ни за что не сблюю.
И так – вплоть до девятой.
А там опять понадобится бутерброд.
highlight.explain: The third sentence gives the reason: without a snack the first dose might make him throw up.
